### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fccbd9d0d5f6637111ec9e3f17a723fe84c6903a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `36a9b5f3d737aea70405a052059f175bd5d1bc53` — the merge of head `a16a9c02bcb59793cc651d78a5c542a87f67cb34` into base `fccbd9d0d5f6637111ec9e3f17a723fe84c6903a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 36a9b5f3d737aea70405a052059f175bd5d1bc53 && git checkout 36a9b5f3d737aea70405a052059f175bd5d1bc53
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fccbd9d0d5f6637111ec9e3f17a723fe84c6903a a16a9c02bcb59793cc651d78a5c542a87f67cb34 && git checkout -B drift-repro fccbd9d0d5f6637111ec9e3f17a723fe84c6903a && git merge --no-ff a16a9c02bcb59793cc651d78a5c542a87f67cb34

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fccbd9d0d5f6637111ec9e3f17a723fe84c6903a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a16a9c02bcb59793cc651d78a5c542a87f67cb34`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md, packages/lint/src/validate-record-title.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx + their string pins and .changeset/25071-composite-title-stored.md

### ① Derived judgments

- **The ADR edit is one hunk inside D3's migration sentence** (`:140-146`). D3's decision, D1, D2, D4, the alternatives and the addendum are byte-unchanged. The new sentence binds exactly the two arms of ruling 6308445871:
  - a composite title that an import, a sort or a search must match is a stored computed field designated `nameField`;
  - a `returnType: 'text'` formula stays legal for a title shown for display only.
- **The shape matches the runtime.** `planStoredExpressions` (`objectql/src/engine.ts:3041-3050`) selects `def.type !== 'formula' && def.expression` on insert (`:16210`) and update (`:17559`). The only virtual-type guard is `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES = new Set(['formula'])` (`spec/src/data/search-fields.ts:96`), used by `assertFilterIsMaterializable` and the import candidate filter (`core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:734-745`). So such a field is an ordinary column for where, sort, search and import, and `packages/rest/src/import-reference-stored-computed-title.test.ts` pins the import side.
- **Strings only.** No rule id, severity, condition, path or export changes. Only string literals move. The hints are 189 and 191 characters and the fix line is 198, all within the 200 bound. Tests change only their expected strings.
- **Non-blocking:**
  - the `title-format-retired` message now carries the whole prescription, and the remedy would sit better in `hint` alone;
  - D3 says "written on write" where item 9 says "when its sources change". The engine recomputes on the owning record's write, so a title over a lookup can go stale. That stays item 9's to carry.

- **Round 2 (`a16a9c02bc`)**, after a Test Core red on `e9e0ec7bab`: `packages/cli/test/data-model-rules.test.ts:291` pins that the `missing-name-field` fix line cites `ADR-0079`, and the first wording had dropped it. The delta against the reviewed head is one string in `data-model-rules.ts:741-742` and its verbatim lint pin. The new line is "Set `nameField` (ADR-0079), never `titleFormat` (`os explain title-format-retired`); a composite title to import/sort/search by is a text field with an `expression` (a text formula is display-only)." It is 198 characters, the meaning is unchanged, and the CLI test is not edited. The dev grepped every other package's tests and found no other pin on the changed strings.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: only diagnostic and `os explain` text change, and nothing a metadata author can write moves. No spec package is touched.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H:** `docs/adr/**` is in the file list. This PASS is not the landing record, and no AI seat approves, queues or arms auto-merge. The PR waits for an APPROVED review from `os-zhuang` or `hotlong`.
- **Follow-up #25129:** the `titleFormat` describe at `spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:2843`, its four generated pages, and `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md:88` and `:90`.
- **Overlap:** PR #25074 also edits `rule-explanations.ts`, in a distant region with no textual conflict.
- **Untouched:** `content/docs/releases/`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-25071-composite-title-stored`
Reviewed-by: `session_01D6F9axfoPzR7t8G1J7Ytzz`
